This means vaccination status affects survival both directly (via reaction) and indirectly (via reaction affecting survival). Method 1 (conditioning on reaction) blocks the indirect path, isolating the direct effect of status on survival. Method 2 (total correlation) sums both direct and indirect effects. Therefore, Method 1 is indeed more correct for isolating the specific effect. My previous failure was likely due to over-analyzing the graph structure or misreading the "direct effect" phrasing. Next time, I will immediately answer "Yes" and explicitly state that Method 1 isolates the direct effect by blocking the mediator (reaction), whereas Method 2 conflates direct and indirect effects.
